chosen.premise: Hitmonchan twists its punches like a drill, letting it punch through concrete walls.
chosen.hook: Hitmonchan does not punch walls—it drills through them.
chosen.visualIdea: A straight punch fails against a concrete wall, then a corkscrew arm motion bores a clean tunnel through it.
chosen.note: A highly specific Hitmonchan-only-feeling contradiction to normal punching, backed by two entries and immediately understandable on screen.

candidates.premise: Hitmonchan twists its punches like a drill, letting it punch through concrete walls.
candidates.hook: Hitmonchan does not punch walls—it drills through them.
candidates.visualIdea: A straight punch fails against a concrete wall, then a corkscrew arm motion bores a clean tunnel through it.
candidates.note: A highly specific Hitmonchan-only-feeling contradiction to normal punching, backed by two entries and immediately understandable on screen.

candidates.premise: Before contact, Hitmonchan spins its arms to increase the strength of every punch move.
candidates.hook: Its secret weapon happens before the punch even lands.
candidates.visualIdea: A power meter rises as Hitmonchan rotates its arms, then surges when the punch connects.
candidates.note: The pre-contact arm spin is distinctive and directly supported, but 'every punch move' makes the claim slightly broader than the source wording.

candidates.premise: Hitmonchan's punches travel so fast that even a slight graze can cause a burn.
candidates.hook: You do not need to be hit by Hitmonchan to get burned.
candidates.visualIdea: A target narrowly avoids a punch, but the passing airflow leaves a glowing burn mark.
candidates.note: Extremely surprising and well supported, though the burn effect may be harder to depict clearly without implying an unsupported game-mechanic status condition.

candidates.premise: Hitmonchan can unleash air-slicing punches, but needs a short break after exactly three minutes of fighting.
candidates.hook: The punching Pokémon has a three-minute battery limit.
candidates.visualIdea: A three-minute fight timer fills as invisible punches fly, then abruptly switches to a rest countdown.
candidates.note: The three-minute constraint is concrete and highly visual, but 'exactly' and 'battery limit' overstate the entries, which say it rests after three minutes.

candidates.premise: Hitmonchan appears motionless while firing lightning-fast punch volleys that cannot be seen.
candidates.hook: What if standing still was actually a rapid-fire attack?
candidates.visualIdea: Hitmonchan stands frozen while impact flashes and a storm of unseen punch trails appear around a target.
candidates.note: Directly supported by multiple Pokédex entries and easy to stage visually, though the premise is more descriptive than mechanically distinctive.

candidates.premise: At level 20, Tyrogue can become Hitmonchan, Hitmonlee, or Hitmontop through the same listed evolution method.
candidates.hook: Level 20 does not decide which fighter Tyrogue becomes.
candidates.visualIdea: A level-20 Tyrogue stands at a three-way crossroads pointing toward Hitmonlee, Hitmonchan, and Hitmontop.
candidates.note: The three-way evolution is clear and visual, but the supplied research only establishes the shared level-20 method, not the actual conditions that determine each outcome.

rounds.request: No stronger angle is required; the chosen angle is specific, surprising, visually demonstrable, and supported by two Pokédex entries.
